entries.title: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All rescued after cruise ship hit by tanker in New Orleans
entries.snippet: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.

entries.title: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage after almost 24 hours of disruption
entries.snippet: Experts say the event is a "stark reminder" of how heavily the world relies on a small group of big tech providers.

entries.title: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?
entries.snippet: Microsoft says it is continuing to restore services including Outlook and Teams following a global outage.

entries.title: Watch: How a server outage took down Microsoft Teams and Outlook
entries.snippet: A Microsoft outage is affecting services including Teams, Outlook and AI software Copilot.

entries.title: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test
entries.snippet: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean.

entries.title: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine
entries.snippet: The fact the question of European security now features in discussions is viewed in Moscow as a victory, BBC Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg says.

entries.title: Nvidia scandal fallout widens as Trump's treasury secretary blames cabinet colleague
entries.snippet: Scott Bessent suggests Howard Lutnick’s commerce department failed to ban exports of Nvidia's chips to a firm thought to have links with China.

entries.title: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own
entries.snippet: Pope Leo XIV is in Peru as part of his Latin America tour, just weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.

entries.title: German spies handed new powers to tackle 'hybrid threats' from abroad
entries.snippet: German reforms mean foreign and domestic intelligence services will have greater powers to combat espionage, terrorism and sabotage.

entries.title: Democratic Senate leader Schumer set to face leadership challenge
entries.snippet: Maryland Senator Van Hollen says "new leadership" is needed for Democrats following the party's recent midterm successes.

entries.title: Aide to fugitive Ukrainian ex-PM wounded in latest Moscow car bombing
entries.snippet: Sergei Zavorotny, now a journalist and commentator, was previously an adviser to Ukrainian ex-prime minister Mykola Azarov.

entries.title: Rosalía scoops historic third best album award at Latin Grammys
entries.snippet: The Spanish singer is recognised for her fourth album Lux which was released last year to rave reviews.

entries.title: African Miss Universe beauty queens in limbo as US visa restrictions bite
entries.snippet: Hall has been seeking a US visa in South Africa as other African beauty queens face similar hurdles.

entries.title: At least 24 killed after bus collides with truck in north-east India
entries.snippet: Several of the deceased are college students, according to local official Atul Bora, but they have not yet been publicly identified.

entries.title: Watch: Cruise ship seen sinking after collision with cargo ship in New Orleans
entries.snippet: All passengers have been accounted for after a cargo ship collided with a docked cruise ship.

entries.title: Watch: Divers explore US ship sunk off Florida coast to create new reef
entries.snippet: The ship was intentionally sunk off the coast of Florida in order to create the world's largest artificial ocean reef.

entries.title: Will the Eurovision Song Contest succeed in Asia?
entries.snippet: The world’s biggest and longest-running song contest is coming to Asia, with eleven countries competing in Bangkok, Thailand on Saturday.

entries.title: Military cemetery decorum: The tradition behind Hegseth's Veterans Day reprimand
entries.snippet: BBC's Bernd Debusmann breaks down why Defence Secretary Hegseth's group was reprimanded at Arlington National Cemetery and the history behind its strict rules of conduct.

entries.title: 'We've got to run': Inside ruined Ukraine power plant under constant drone threat
entries.snippet: Dan Johnson visits one of the country's largest power stations, barely left standing after a ballistic missile strike by Russia.

entries.title: Hegseth and advisers reprimanded by guard at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
entries.snippet: Following a ceremony marking Veterans Day, a group that included Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth was shouted at to be quiet.

entries.title: DHS head Markwayne Mullin says there is not a threat to the U.S. amid FAA ground stop
entries.snippet: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin spoke to at the White House on Friday afternoon after the FAA issues a total ground stop. NPR was there for the briefing.

entries.title: Stuck on the tarmac without information: Travelers share their ground stop experiences
entries.snippet: Passengers stuck on airplanes on tarmacs across the country during the FAA ground stop on Friday share their stories.

entries.title: GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
entries.snippet: Some Republican state officials are reviving a bid for mail-in voting restrictions for the 2028 election by appealing a court order blocking the Postal Service from carrying out a revised ballot rule.

entries.title: FAA issues nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports
entries.snippet: The FAA has issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following a "communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers," according to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.

entries.title: With his challenge to Schumer, Van Hollen forces a debate over Democrats' mandate
entries.snippet: Democrats say they have a mandate to deliver change, but as the party gets ready to retake the majority in both the House and Senate, there are divides over who should lead it.

entries.title: The government says it will close a beloved D.C. park Sunday. Will a judge step in?
entries.snippet: Federal judge Ana Reyes grilled the government on Friday about its plans for East Potomac Park, and indicated she could order it to remain open despite President Trump's renovation wishes.

entries.title: What's Trump's strategy now with Iran? To keep things as they are
entries.snippet: President Trump says the "status quo" is what Gulf Arab allies want as the Iran war hits a stalemate and the U.S. midterms force a pivot from threats of attacks to economic pressure.

entries.title: The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue
entries.snippet: Election officials are preparing for the Trump administration's pressure tactics over potential noncitizens on state voter rolls to continue, though recent court rulings pose new obstacles.

entries.title: Does Europe regret its bet on U.S. defense?
entries.snippet: Europe bet big on American defense technology and they're now paying the price. Years-long backlogs are underway due to production delays and the U.S. own military needs.

entries.title: How Sen. Chris Van Hollen plans to flex Democratic power on the foreign aid front
entries.snippet: He's the ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee that oversees health aid and he's just announced he's running for Majority Leader. He spoke to NPR about his foreign aid vision.

entries.title: SpaceX's Starship soars into orbit after booster malfunction thwarts double catch attempt
entries.snippet: SpaceX's attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the launch pad was thwarted when the booster malfunctioned and ended up in the water Friday, but the spacecraft still soared into orbit in its boldest test yet.

entries.title: FAA issues rare nationwide ground stop due to 'extraordinary circumstances'
entries.snippet: Air travel across the country came to a standstill on Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop citing "extraordinary circumstances" and "reasons of safety." Aviation correspondent Miles O'Brien reports.

entries.snippet: Sales of existing homes in the U.S. fell last month to their lowest level in more than 16 years. That's according to a new report by the National Association of Realtors. In October alone, sales dropped to 3.75 million homes, an 8.8% drop compared with the same time last year. St

entries.title: Does Van Hollen have enough support to beat Schumer in Senate leadership race?
entries.snippet: Senate Democrats won back their majority last week, and now they're fighting over who will lead it. Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen has thrown his hat in the ring and says he will take on current Democratic leader Chuck Schumer. Congressional correspondent Lisa Desjardins reports

entries.title: ICE touts record number of deportations in agency's history
entries.snippet: The Department of Homeland Security reports that immigrant deportations and arrests hit an all-time high. More than 491,000 people were arrested by ICE in the last fiscal year, and more than 483,000 were deported. The Trump administration has said it aims to deport one million im

entries.title: What to know about Microsoft's outage and why it takes so long to restore email services
entries.snippet: Unlike modern web apps or authentication gatekeepers, email wasn't designed to fail fast, meaning to immediately halt when a problem arises.

entries.title: Brooks and Marcus on how Republicans are responding to midterm losses
entries.snippet: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Ruth Marcus of The New Yorker join Amna Nawaz to discuss the week in politics, including the fallout of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and what the Trump administration knew, how Republicans are responding to their losses in the midterm ele

entries.snippet: Anthony Roth Costanzo cuts an unusual figure in the world of music. The leading international opera singer is performing in the Metropolitan Opera's critically acclaimed and wildly popular "Lincoln at the Bardo," which the Met will stream for free to the public on Saturday. Senio

entries.title: WATCH: Homeland Security Secretary Mullin says FAA flight stoppage 'isn't another 9/11'
entries.snippet: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there are no indications of an attack against the nation, after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights nationwide Friday afternoon due to communications problems.

entries.title: U.S. wrongly withheld New York highway funds over immigrant licenses, appeals court rules
entries.snippet: The U.S. Transportation Department wrongly decided to withhold nearly $74 million in highway money from New York state after it refused to revoke nearly 33,000 questionable commercial driver's licenses for immigrants when an audit revealed problems last year, a federal appeals co

entries.title: FAA grounds all flights at U.S. airports due to air traffic control communications problems
entries.snippet: The nation's top homeland security official attributed the problem to a telecommunications outage and said there was no indication yet of a nefarious act.

entries.title: GOP Rep. Lauren Boebert of Colorado loses U.S. House seat to Democrat Eileen Laubacher
entries.snippet: Democrat Eileen Laubacher defeated Rep. Lauren Boebert for a Colorado U.S. House seat on Friday, ousting a three-term Republican and staple of conservative media.

entries.title: Rescues operations underway in New Orleans after tanker hits river cruise boat
entries.snippet: A tanker struck a New Orleans river cruise with 129 passengers on board on Friday, partially submerging the boat. Rescues were underway on the Mississippi River, officials say.

entries.title: WATCH: Brooklyn community leaders, residents hold meeting on building collapse
entries.snippet: New York officials, from building inspectors to prosecutors, say they're investigating what caused the three-story building to come crashing down as workers were digging at an adjacent construction site. Those who lost family, neighbors and their homes demanded answers.

entries.title: UN chief says 'immediate and drastic' emissions cuts needed to avert climate change catastrophe
entries.snippet: "You cannot build peace on a burning planet," United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres told reporters, stressing that climate change is central to the U.N.'s work because it contributes to geopolitical instability.

entries.title: Supreme Court will consider Trump's executive order suspending asylum access at the southern border
entries.snippet: The Trump administration is asking the justices to overturn lower court decisions that found it was illegal to block asylum applications following an executive order that called the situation at the southern border an "invasion."

entries.title: UK police launch sex offense investigation into children's author and TV personality David Walliams
entries.snippet: The Metropolitan Police said it had received a number of allegations of past abuse following the joint investigation this week by ITV News and the Guardian newspaper.

entries.title: 'TrumpCare' and commemorative plaques — how Democrats are pitching deal-making with the president
entries.snippet: Some Democrats who swept into power by riding voter backlash to Trump are now pitching ways to collaborate with the president, playing to his vanity and his love of making deals to propel their own agenda.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Tanker collides with cruise ship on Mississippi in New Orleans
entries.snippet: A freighter collided with a cruise ship carrying around 130 people in New Orleans, causing the paddlewheel vessel to capsize. More than 30 people were hospitalized, but all passengers survived and were accounted for.

entries.title: Ukraine updates: EU to send united front to potential peace talks
entries.snippet: Germany, France, the UK, Italy and Poland — as well as the EU itself — will jointly represent Europe in possible peace talks. Meanwhile, a second car bomb in two days has exploded in Moscow. DW has more.

entries.title: David Walliams: UK police launch sex offense probe into comedian
entries.snippet: The "Little Britain" star and "Britain's Got Talent" judge has been accused of engaging in sexual misconduct and inappropriate behavior towards young women and girls. Walliams denies the allegations.

entries.title: Pope Leo celebrates Mass in his former diocese of Chiclayo, Peru
entries.snippet: Over a million people have gathered for Mass with Pope Leo XIV on Friday. The event in northern Peru, where he served as bishop before becoming head of the Catholic Church, is the centerpiece of his South American tour.

entries.title: The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture
entries.snippet: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

entries.title: EU leaders urged to 'act now' to stay AI competitive with US, China
entries.snippet: EU leaders in Dublin were called on by an AI executive to move quickly in the tech race with the US and China. EU official Metsola, however, expressed frustration with the idea that the bloc is behind in AI development.

entries.title: What's going on with the polar vortex?
entries.snippet: Observations show the ring of fierce winds that rotate at the Earth's North Pole has changed direction. Scientists say it's a historic disruption and the earliest reversal on record. What could it mean for the weather?

entries.title: Ice hockey: Russia threatens against Canada and Germany over exclusion from tournaments
entries.snippet: A fortnight after the CAS ordered ice hockey's governing body to reintegrate Russia into international play, a solution remains elusive. Now Russia has threatened to take legal action against two tournament hosts.

entries.title: Why does El Salvador's Bukele have troops in Haiti?
entries.snippet: Haiti's Prime Minister congratulating El Salvador's President for a gang crackdown in Haiti has shone a light on the relationship between the two countries. What's going on, and where does the US stand?

entries.title: Iran targeted US radar system in Bahrain
entries.snippet: Iran claimed it struck US radar systems in Bahrain, while the US said it had intercepted the attacks. Clashes continue in the Strait of Hormuz, as the war remains in a state of de-escalation.

entries.title: Beijing faces its Russia dilemma amid talk of Xi-Trump-Putin summit
entries.snippet: China is forced to tread carefully as it considers hosting a meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, and Donald Trump. While the optics are sure to favor Moscow, Beijing is risking its image at the global stage.

entries.title: Cyber attacks and hybrid warfare: Germany gives sweeping powers to its police and intelligence services
entries.snippet: Drone sightings and cyberattacks have heightened security concerns. How are the police preparing to meet these challenges? And how do intelligence services plan to counter threats from both domestic and foreign sources?

entries.title: Indonesia's wiretapping scandal opens a political fault line
entries.snippet: Senior police officers are accused of illegally monitoring President Prabowo Subianto, exposing rival networks within Indonesia's security establishment and renewing concerns about political misuse of surveillance.

entries.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
entries.snippet: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms has cast doubt on Anthropic's looming IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.

entries.title: Germany's Nmecha won't repeat controversial goal celebration
entries.snippet: Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp says that midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a goal celebration that sparked controversy over the past week. Germany are set to face Serbia and the Netherlands in the Nations League.

entries.title: Humanitarian situation in Gaza worsens amid political deadlock
entries.snippet: In war-battered Gaza, heavy rain flooded and damaged thousands of tents. Several people died. Could pressure by Trump's Board of Peace on Israel and Hamas help to ease the humanitarian crisis amid stalled peace talks?

entries.title: Germany news: Parliament agrees on debt-laden 2027 budget
entries.snippet: The budget committee in the Bundestag worked into the night to sign off on next year's spending plans. These include levels of new debt only eclipsed once, at the height of the COVID pandemic. DW has more.

entries.title: Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
entries.snippet: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.

entries.title: After suffering its worst election result, what's next for the ANC — and for South Africa?
entries.snippet: A crushing local election result across the country has left South Africa's ruling ANC searching for answers. Experts say the vote reflects public frustration with service delivery failures — signaling a political shift.
